Header:
Date: 2026-12-29T16:00:00Z
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Atlas - Head of ML), Ravi Gupta (Atlas - Platform Eng), Sofia Lopez (Atlas - Security)

Summary (auto): quick Optimize walkthrough concentrating on batching and caching; agreed pilot and docs to follow.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Ava): Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Ava, AE at Redwood, and Diego is our SE.
00:12 Diego (SE): Hi team, thanks for the time. We know Atlas is trying to keep P95 under ~120ms on chat while cutting token cost by ~40%, so today we'll focus on batching and prefix/KV cache recommendations and show the cost model.
00:30 Maya (Atlas): Yeah that's right. Our current stack is in-house endpoints on GCP, mixed GPUs, and we see pretty variable latencies. We also have strict data residency and KMS requirements.
00:45 Ravi: we're also worried about tail latency when traffic spikes, and how caching might affect freshness.
00:55 Diego: totally; we'll walk through continuous batching first — how it increases token throughput by grouping requests within a short micro-batching window — and the tradeoff: slight added latency for significantly lower per-token cost.
01:15 Diego: for our sample workload, with a 10ms batching window we saw 25% cost savings, with P95 up ~10ms; at 30ms window it was 40% savings but P95 moved up ~35ms.
01:40 Maya: ok that math helps. Do you have numbers for short prompts vs long context?
01:50 Diego: yes — short prompts benefit more from batching overhead amortization. For long-context chat where generation dominates, batching still helps but less so. We'll put the spreadsheet in the follow-up.
02:15 Speaker 2 (Maya): can you explain prefix cache vs KV cache? I always mix those up.
02:25 Diego: sure — prefix cache (also called prefix/KV-cache hybrid sometimes) caches model activations for common prefixes, so if many users start with the same instruction or system prompt, you reuse the cached KV state and don't recompute those tokens; it's lowest-latency and high hit-rate when your app has repeated prompts.
02:50 Diego: KV cache (we mean per-conversation KV cache) is storing previously computed key/value tensors per session; it's great for multi-turn chat where the conversation grows — you avoid re-encoding the whole history and only compute new tokens. Prefix cache is more cross-request reuse, KV cache is per-session continuation.
03:10 Sofia (Security): how do you handle encrypted KV/prefix cache? We need KMS integration and audit logs, can't have plaintext persisted.
03:20 Ava: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM options; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can rotate keys. We'll attach SOC2 and KMS docs. Cache entries can be encrypted at rest and we surface audit logs in Console.
03:40 Ravi: if we use prefix caching heavily, what's the storage and eviction policy? We have limited in-memory and want predictable costs.
03:50 Diego: good Q — policies are LRU-based with size and TTL controls. You can pin hot prefixes and we expose metrics in Console showing hit rates and memory. We recommend starting with a 24-72 hour TTL for instruction/system prompts, adjust after observing hit rates.
04:15 Diego: on cost model — we walked through token unit economics: base per-token infer cost + memory/kv overhead + amortized batching benefit. For Atlas' sample traffic, our model shows ~38% cost reduction using moderate batching + prefix caching with a 15ms window and 40% prefix hit rate.
04:45 Maya: what about quality regressions when switching quantized or smaller variants during fallback? We can't accept hallucination spikes.
04:55 Diego: we recommend running evals against a held-out prompt set; Optimize's quality monitor ties to prompt sets and will alert regression. For fallbacks, we prefer routing to compatible model variants with verified performance profiles and to do canarying.
05:20 Speaker 3 (Ravi): what's the lift to run the pilot? We need a timeline and what ATLAS must provide.
05:30 Ava: next steps — we propose a 1-week perf pilot: Atlas provides anonymized traces and 50k sample requests; Redwood runs benchmarks on Hosted and Dedicated variants; SE shares cost-model spreadsheet and ops runbook.
05:50 Maya: sounds fair. On Dedicated vs Hosted — if we pick Dedicated, how much does that change batching behavior?
06:00 Diego: Dedicated gives you a predictable GPU pool so batching windows and throughput are more consistent; hosted is multi-tenant so variance is slightly higher but Redwood routes by policy. For tight SLOs Dedicated + autoscaling policies gives the most predictable P95.
06:25 Sofia: also need SSO/SAML integration and RBAC for Console access.
06:30 Ava: yes, we support SSO/SAML, SCIM, fine-grained RBAC; we'll share the security checklist.
06:40 Diego: here's a small gotcha — prefix caching hit rates depend heavily on prompt standardization. If you have many unique system prompts per user, hit rate drops. So centralizing the system prompt and canonicalizing user inputs raises hit rate fast.
07:00 Maya: we've got variable system prompts, but could move to a templated system prompt.
07:10 Diego: for KV cache sizing: estimate KV memory as roughly N_tokens * model_kv_size * active_sessions. We'll give a quick calc in the spreadsheet; for example, with 100k active sessions and 1k average tokens per session that becomes large — in that case you want aggressive TTLs and eviction or Dedicated with larger memory.
07:35 Ravi: any difference for embeddings workloads?
07:40 Diego: embeddings don't use KV cache; batching still helps for throughput but caching strategy is different — you cache embedding vectors for repeated inputs.
07:50 Maya: can we get a sample of the cost-model spreadsheet?
07:55 Ava: yes Diego will send it, and it'll include scenarios for different batch windows, prefix hit rates, and Dedicated vs Hosted costings.
08:05 Diego: quick demo: (screen-share) here's Console — Optimize tab shows suggested batch window, recommended quantization profile, and a simulated cost delta. You can flip prefix cache on/off and see estimated hit rate impact.
08:35 Diego: note the Console also surfaces tracing per-route and token-level cost; you can drill into slow requests and see whether KV cache or batching was effective.
08:50 Sofia: about audit logs and retention — we need 12 months for audit; can Console stream logs to our ELK?
08:58 Ava: yes, we support log export to S3/Cloud Storage or direct SIEM integrations. We'll include retention options in the security docs.
09:10 Maya: how long does it take to enable prefix caching in a private deployment?
09:15 Diego: with Redwood Private it can be part of the deployment; typical lead time is a couple weeks for onboarding and key integrations. For hosted you can flip caching on per-route pretty quickly — minutes to hours depending on route configs.
09:35 Ravi: what about data residency — some EU traffic must stay in EU.
09:40 Ava: we can route requests regionally and dedicate capacity in EU; we'll include region mapping in the follow-up.
09:50 Maya: ok let's recap.
10:00 Ava: recap: 1) Atlas to share anonymized traces and sample prompts; 2) Redwood SE to run 1-week pilot on Hosted and Dedicated, produce cost model spreadsheet; 3) Redwood to send SOC2/KMS/VPC docs and Dedicated pricing; 4) schedule benchmark week (target: week of Jan 5).
10:25 Maya: agree. We'll send traces by Jan 4.
10:30 Ava: thanks everyone — Diego will send the spreadsheet and runbook.
10:35 Diego: thanks, will send and set up the perf run details.
10:40 Meeting end.
